newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan asks banks to form fund management firms.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan asks banks to form fund management firms.

text.p: The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) has told banks to conduct their fund management and investment advisory services through separate subsidiaries from January 1, 1997.

"Banks desiring to provide fund management and other investment advisory services shall be allowed to do so through subsidiary companies formed by them under the laws of Pakistan for the exclusive purpose of undertaking fund management activities," said an SBP circular received on Wednesday.
SBP said the new regulation would take effect on January 1 and would supersede earlier ones on fund management services.
It said new contracts for fund management should be undertaken only through subsidiaries formed for the purpose.
The central bank gave no reason for the change, but bankers said it would force banks to disclose their assets and liabilities under fund management activities.
Bankers said foreign commercial banks and some local investment banks were managing four to five billion rupees ($100-$125 million) of funds for individuals and companies.
These funds are not clearly disclosed in their balance sheets and the new regulation will therefore affect their capital requirement ratios as well as their balance sheets.

The SBP said the minimum paid-up capital of new fund management subsidiaries should be 100 million rupees. The parent bank's contribution must be at least 51 percent of the subsidiary's paid-up capital.
It said the fund management subsidiary would be set up with a binding commitment to offer a maximum of 49 percent of their paid-up shares to the public within three years of their launch.
Bankers complained that setting up new fund management units would add to their costs and said the deadline was too short.
